title: A link to a large T12 orbit runs the whole representation build in the island's hydration task: a long task of 51 to 103 ms at full speed, where a pick of the same node has none
location: site/src/components/tools/t12/model.ts:575 (admitLink validates with new T12Tool(configOf(state), { defer: true, need: 'staged' })); site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:583-604 (readLink, called in the hydration $effect) and :548-549 (load builds a second T12Tool with need 'staged'); site/src/components/tools/t12/model.ts:194-216 (representationOf 'staged': startRepresentation, addMatrices and addSignedMoves for every node at once in one call)
claim: When a T12 state comes from a link (/tools/rep/?g=..&k=.., or a lesson instance's prefixed keys), the hydration task runs minusculeNodes, orbitSize, play, minusculeMatrices and signedMoves of every node together. The same work after a pick runs one engine call per task (build() then representationSteps). So the hydration task is a long task at full speed on every built orbit of about 240 positions or more.
expected: SPEC 7.6 'Main-thread work': 'No engine call on the main thread may become a long task (50 ms) on that phone.' The builders' record decisions/P5-A2.md commits T12 to 'A pick builds the representation one engine call per task (decide, enumerate, sign, ...)' and 'above 300 positions the signed moves take one task per node'. A link reaches the same states (any pick's Copy link) and should keep the same split.
observed: Chromium 141, 360x800, 1x (no slowdown), 4 CPUs, Node 22.22.0, load 0.98 to 3.49, 5 runs each. The hydration task (the long task during which the island's ssr attribute is removed) has medians: E7 node 6 (756 positions) 65 ms [56, 57, 65, 80, 86]; C8 node 7 (1024) 81 ms [67, 79, 81, 85, 103]; B8 node 7 (1024) 68 ms [64, 67, 68, 70, 79]; D8 node 3 (448) 59 ms [52, 57, 59, 64, 69]; E8 node 8 (240) 51 ms [0, 0, 51, 54, 60]. With 3 runs: E6 node 4 56 ms and D7 node 5 61 ms. The same nodes reached by picks have no long task in any of those runs (median 0; one 53 ms task in 25 pick runs). Controls by link on the same boards with small orbits (E7 node 7, D8 node 1, B8 node 1, A2 node 2) have no long task in 12 runs. At 4x (phone-like): E7 node 6 link hydration 294, 299 and 352 ms against 89 to 131 ms for the longest task after a pick; E8 node 8 197 to 345 ms against 0 to 69. A source-mapped CPU profile of the C8 node 7 link at 1x puts readLink, admitLink, the T12Tool constructor and representationOf inside the hydration task (121 to 142 ms with profiler overhead). Inside it, addMatrices calls minusculeMatrices (34.5 ms sampled) and addSignedMoves calls signedMoves for all 8 nodes (10.8 ms sampled). T12.spec.ts 'no long task when E6/E7 is picked' tests picks only, so the gate's tests do not see this path.

specRef: SPEC.md 7.6 'Main-thread work' ('No engine call on the main thread may become a long task (50 ms) on that phone'); SPEC 5.1 E-9; decisions/P5-A2.md (the entry on the relation list and the pick steps; 'A pick builds the representation one engine call per task'); lens attack 22
proposedFix: Validate the link in admitLink and build the state in load() with need 'facts'. When the link's board or node differs from the configured one, run the same representationSteps as build() (one engine call per task, signed moves one node per task above 300 positions) before the panels are drawn. Add a link case to T12.spec.ts's long-task tests.

Also read DECISIONS.md, decisions/P5-A2.md, reports/gate-G5.md (gate commit line names 006f50d), the phase 5 review and repair JSONs, the phase 4 RT-07 output, RT-07 lens attacks 22 and 24 and its section 6, and P5-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS 'Known and decided'. Code at 006f50d confirms the cause. model.ts:575: admitLink validates with new T12Tool(configOf(state), {defer: true, need: 'staged'}). model.ts:211-213: in the browser, 'staged' runs addMatrices (minusculeMatrices) and addSignedMoves for every node synchronously. T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:600-604: the hydration $effect calls readLink, which calls admitLink and then load(), which builds T12Tool again with 'staged'. build() (:520-545) instead runs representationSteps (model.ts:150-176), one engine call per task and one task per node above 300 positions. model.ts:186 documents 'staged' as 'a state loaded after hydration', but readLink runs inside hydration. T12.spec.ts:907 tests long tasks only for picks. On the two held items: (1) the E-9 sizing the owner holds covers 1120 and 1792 positions (B8, C8, D8 nodes 4 and 5) and the size of one call. The finding's nodes have 240 to 1024 positions (E8:8, D8:3, E6:4, D7:5, E7:6, B8:7, C8:7). Its controls isolate grouping as the cause: picks of the same nodes have no long task at 1x, and links to small orbits have none. (2) The lab acceptance concerns Lighthouse TBT figures in the G3 range. This finding compares per-task measurements against pick and small-orbit controls on the same machine, not a lab figure. Strongest counter-record: DECISIONS.md 'RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf: what the residual of P3-RT-07-02 was' ('SPEC 7.6 ... says only that no engine call ... may become a long task; it does not say how a tool's load should be shaped when hydration itself is long') and 'MERGE: red-team round 1, residual fixes' ('The load is still one long task ... which is Svelte's hydration and render ..., not engine work; SPEC 7.6 bounds engine calls'). Those records accepted a long task only because it was not engine work, with about 30 ms of engine work in it. Their board-load.spec entry treats 'no task's share of engine work reaches 50 ms' as the property checked. Here the extra task time is the engine work that the link path groups.
refute.reason: not refuted: the cause is neither held item (it is not the owner's E-9 sizing of minusculeMatrices on the 1120- and 1792-position orbits, and not the machine-bound lab TBT) but a link load that runs in the hydration task what a pick splits into one engine call per task. R1 fails: no sentence of 7.6, 7.4 or E-9 permits grouping engine calls into one long hydration task, and the P3 residual record accepted a long load task only because it was Svelte work, not engine work. R2 fails: the finding quotes 7.6 correctly, but there is a real ambiguity for the owner. 7.6 literally bounds 'an engine call', and at 1x the finding's largest single call (minusculeMatrices on C8 node 7, 34.5 ms sampled with profiler overhead) is under 50 ms. The project's own records, though (P5-A2 pick split and 'hydration computes the facts only'; the P3 residual 'task's share of engine work'), read the bound per task. R3 fails: T12 is phase 5 at gate G5. R4 fails: the oracle has nothing on timing. R5 fails: 7.6 is [D], but no record makes a link load an exception; P5-A2's hydration record says the opposite. R6 fails: there is no record in gate-G5.md, the phase 5 reviews or earlier rounds. Major fits 'a behaviour the specification states is missing or wrong'.

title: T12 classifies the same board three times on every pick: the steps of a pick resolve the board in three tasks, which defeats resolveBoard's per-microtask reuse
location: site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:534 (defaultNode(resolveBoard(spec)) in the first step of build); site/src/components/tools/t12/model.ts:200 (representationOf -> startRepresentation(resolveBoard(spec)) in a later step); site/src/components/tools/t12/model.ts:409 (the T12Tool constructor's resolveBoard in load, after the steps); site/src/lib/state.ts:259-271 (resolvedThisRun is cleared at the next microtask, the RT-FIX P3-RT-07-02 mechanism)
claim: T12 spreads a pick over several tasks, as SPEC 7.6 requires, and resolves the board in three of them. resolveBoard reuses a board object only within one microtask run, so each task gets a new object, and resolveBoard and the engine's guards classify each new object (E-11 caches per object).
expected: SPEC 5.6, last sentence: 'A tool decides whether a board is of finite type by calling classify once when the board is loaded.' Every other tool measured in the phase 4 round classifies a picked board once (T10's extra computations are sub-boards inside the engine).
observed: A DevTools logpoint on classifyUncached (source-map build): pick E6 3 computations (n=6: 3), E7 3, D4 3, B8 3, G2 3, and C8 after a link load 3. Load of /tools/rep/ 1. Load of M8 1. The link load ?g=E7&k=6 makes 2 (the default A2 once, E7 once), the reading the phase 4 round accepted. One computation costs 0.09 to 0.37 ms in Node (redteam-RT-07-p5-rep.test.ts), so no long task results, which is why this is minor.
reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline; npm run build; then, in site/: OUT_DIR=/tmp/rt07-maps npx astro build --config ../redteam/astro.sourcemap.config.mjs; then from the root: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mutation-game/03d88ee7-3b55-5f84-9822-84f78aad9733/scratchpad/pw-browsers node redteam/redteam-RT-07-classify-count-p5.mjs /tmp/rt07-maps 5370. It exits 1 and lists 'pick E6 3 {"n=6":3}' and the others.
specRef: SPEC.md 5.6 (last sentence); SPEC 5.1 E-11; lens attack 24; sibling of the fix of P3-RT-07-02 (resolvedThisRun in lib/state.ts)
proposedFix: Resolve the board once per pick and pass the object through the steps and into load(), for example by caching per generation instead of per microtask, or by keeping the board object on the representation.

refute.citation: SPEC.md 5.6, last sentence (unlabelled; 5.6 has no [D]): 'A tool decides whether a board is of finite type by calling `classify` once when the board is loaded, never by running an enumeration into its cap.' SPEC.md 5.1 E-11: the verdict is kept in a WeakMap keyed by board object. This supports the finding's expected value.
refute.evidence: Read 5.6 whole and E-11 at 006f50d. The 5.6 sentence has no 'may' or 'unless'. The finding's quote drops the closing clause 'never by running an enumeration into its cap', which does not change the 'once'. The records read 'once' as a count per load. decisions/P2-A7.md 'the verdict cache in state.ts': resolveBoard 'calls classify once' (reason SPEC 5.6). site/src/lib/state.ts:220-228 (the resolvedThisRun comment): 'A tool loads its board in one such run ... one classify per load. The map is emptied in a microtask'. P3-RT-07-02 was confirmed on this reading in round 1 and fixed (DECISIONS.md 'MERGE: red-team round 1, group B': 'one classify per load'). Code: a T12 pick is spread over tasks by design (decisions/P5-A2.md, 'A pick builds the representation one engine call per task'). In those tasks resolveBoard runs at T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:534 (defaultNode(resolveBoard(spec))), model.ts:157 or :200 (startRepresentation(resolveBoard(spec))) and model.ts:409 (the T12Tool constructor in load()). resolvedThisRun is cleared at the next microtask (state.ts:265), so each task builds a new object and verdictOf classifies it. Nothing at 006f50d records an exception for multi-task loads: P5-A2.md mentions resolveBoard only as part of the hydration cost. state-classify-once.test.ts has no T12 case, and T12.test.ts and T12.spec.ts do not count classify.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 fails, because 5.6 has no qualifier allowing more than one classify per load. R2 fails, because a board pick is a board load and the project's records (P2-A7, the resolvedThisRun comment, the confirmed P3-RT-07-02) read 'once' as a count. R3 fails: T12 is phase 5 at G5 and 5.6 applies from phase 2. R4 fails: this is not a mathematical value. R5 fails: 5.6 is not [D], and P5-A2 records the pick split but not repeated classification. R6 fails: there is no open record, and no regression test covers T12. Severity stays as claimed: the rubric is silent on a repeated internal computation that has no observable effect, and the lens's attack 24 rates this case minor.
